title: The notes-app battery on macOS, version 2: the same measurements, gated on the document being on screen and the scroll moving it
note: Frozen before any run against it, unlike version 1, which was written down after the 2026-08-16 run.
Adds the two correctness cells the comparison corpus requires (IC-822, tests 1744-1746, K-322):
content-readiness and input-integrity. The kit measures them with scripts/content_probe.swift, which
reads the document's own lines off each app's window with the system's text recognition. A pair that
fails either contributes no performance value: analyze.py leaves it out and audit.py fails the run.

cells.name: content-readiness
cells.unit: yes or no, per app and workload
cells.definition: the benchmark document's own lines are read off the app's window after it opens, not only a window shown

cells.name: input-integrity
cells.unit: yes or no, per app and workload
cells.definition: the controlled scroll moved the document: the last line read on screen is further down after the scroll than before

cells.name: app-file-size
cells.definition: the app file itself, not its installed footprint

cells.name: memory-50k
cells.definition: resident memory with a 50,000-line document open, summed across processes

cells.name: warm-start-50k
cells.definition: time from launch to a visible window, second and later launches, 50,000 lines

cells.name: idle-cpu-50k
cells.definition: CPU with the document open and nothing happening, 50,000 lines

cells.name: scroll-pacing
cells.definition: p50 and p99 frame interval while scrolling; Krate only, no comparison instrument exists on macOS

cells.name: energy-scroll-leg
cells.definition: energy drawn over the scroll leg, from the platform power meter
